instantiated_cells.justification: Employer expenditure statements are filed only with the updated registration statements due January, May, and September (a tri-annual schedule), not annually.
The statute requires employer expenditure statements to be filed with tri-annual updated registrations (Jan/May/Sep), not monthly.
The only periodic filing times specified for employer expenditure statements are tied to the updated registration deadlines (Jan/May/Sep), leaving no other alternative frequency option.
Employer expenditure statements are due Jan/May/Sep (every four months), not on a quarterly (every three months) schedule.
The statute sets tri-annual updated registration deadlines with accompanying expenditure statements, not semi-annual reporting.
Employers must file expenditure statements with updated registrations due the last day of January, May, and September each year (three times per year).
Employer filings require name and business address but do not require disclosure of whether the employer is public or private or the nature of its business.
Employer expenditure statements expressly exclude 'the compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures to be reported by employers.
Employer expenditure statements require reporting of expenditures (and, when applicable, recipient and other details) but do not require reporting of lobbying contacts.

The employer’s initial registration statement must include a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates, which is information about the issues lobbied in general terms.

Because 'expenditure' includes gifts and items of value such as food, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and employers must report expenditures, these categories are required components when applicable.
Employers must report the 'total amount of expenditures' they made (excluding office facilities and agent compensation), which captures non-compensation (indirect) lobbying-related spending.
Registration requires the legislative agent’s business address but does not require a phone number for the contracted lobbyist.

Employer registration statements identify the legislative agent by name, and employers with multiple agents must include information regarding all legislative agents engaged in their updated registration.
The employer registration/expenditure/financial-transaction statements do not require disclosure of major financial contributors to the employer.
Employer filings must include the employer’s 'name and business address' but do not require a phone number.

Updated registration statements must 'list[] the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated' during the period, which are specific bill/resolution identifiers linked to the employer engagement.
An employer’s statement must show the 'total amount of expenditures' made by the employer during the reporting period.
Employer spending reports do not include salary/fees paid to lobbyists because 'expenditures' for employers exclude 'the compensation paid to legislative agents.'

Employer statements are required to report the total amount of expenditures made, but itemized recipient-level details are mandated only in division (B) for legislative agents, not for employers under division (C).
When a trade association is the employer, the statute explicitly says the statement need not list each member’s name/address, so member/sponsor listings are not required.
Employer registration statements (initial and updated) identify the legislative agent(s) engaged by the employer, effectively listing the lobbyists employed/retained.
